On the existing RTX PRO 4500 Blackwell GPU, median warm inference for eight tested hypotheses was 0.244 s for S32N and 0.402 s for S64N. Peak allocated memory across the candidate-scaling runs was 1.06 GiB. Timings include screening, transfer, scoring and tail calculation, and exclude loading and database writes. They describe the saved window, not end-to-end service guarantees. The same configuration required 0.316 ms per window for PCA and 2.137 ms for GDN in batched comparator evaluation. These baseline timings use a different batching regime and are reported as measured, not as a hardware-independent speedup. The final neural training records total 0.605 GPU hours, excluding tuning, pilot work and experiment inference. Base windows use a 32-sample stride, corresponding to 32 s for the simulator and SKAB and 160 min for Intel. Controlled tests subsample these windows. Native SKAB evaluation retains the full test sequence at that stride. The stride and eight-step target interval limit temporal resolution.
